brackets.section: R.C. 5747.02(A)(3)(c), taxable years beginning in 2026 and after
brackets.note: The statute for 2026 reads: no tax if Ohio taxable nonbusiness income is $26,050 or less, otherwise $332.00 plus 2.75% of the amount over $26,050. One schedule for all filing statuses. The $332 is entered as a lump sum on the second bracket, so tax jumps from $0 to $332 when income crosses $26,050, as the statute says. Disagreement between official sources: the Department of Taxation's 2026 IT 1040ES worksheet prints the 2025 table ($342.00 plus 2.75% up to $100,000, then $2,394.32 plus 3.125%). The statute, the Legislative Service Commission analysis of H.B. 96, Tax Foundation and PolicyEngine all give the single 2.75% bracket with the $332 base for 2026, so the statute is used. H.B. 96 suspended inflation indexing of the brackets for 2025 and 2026 per the LSC analysis, so $26,050 is unchanged. Recheck against the 2026 IT 1040 instructions once published.

earnedIncomeCredit.note: "a nonrefundable credit" that "shall equal thirty per cent of the federal credit allowed for the taxable year" and cannot exceed the tax left after earlier nonrefundable credits. No carryforward.
earnedIncomeCredit.name: Ohio earned income credit

personalExemption.note: Rule: the exemption per person (filer, spouse and each dependent) depends on Ohio modified AGI: $2,400 at $40,000 or less, $2,150 above $40,000 up to $80,000, $1,900 above $80,000, and nothing at $500,000 or more for 2026. The entered amounts are the $2,400 tier. Because one schedule has to cover filer and dependents, the tiers are entered as fractions of $2,400: 2150/2400 above $40,000 and 1900/2400 above $80,000. Multiply out and round to the dollar. Where each part comes from: the tier boundaries are in the statute and in the 2025 IT 1040 booklet, both read directly. The three indexed amounts were read in the 2025 booklet (which shows $0 at $750,000 or greater, the 2025 cutoff). For 2026, the statute read directly gives the $500,000 cutoff and only the unindexed base amounts ($2,350, $2,100, $1,850). The 2026 IT 1040ES worksheet confirms $1,900 and zero at $500,000 or more. That $2,400 and $2,150 carry over to 2026 rests on the LSC analysis saying H.B. 96 suspended indexing for 2025 and 2026, plus Tax Foundation's 2026 table (footnote dd) and PolicyEngine, so the group stays secondary until the 2026 IT 1040 booklet is published. Basis: modified AGI is Ohio AGI (IT 1040 line 3) plus the business income deduction, which equals Ohio AGI for a filer with no business income. The agiLimit is on the same modified AGI, and the exemption is lost at $500,000 or more, one dollar earlier than an 'above $500,000' reading.

rules.note: The joint filing credit details are from PolicyEngine. Columbus's 2.5% is from Tax Foundation's table. Contribution flags checked on 2026-11-12 against PolicyEngine US 2.118.6 (oracle/flags.py), which moves this state's tax by the same amount as this engine for 401k, HSA, IRA and health premium contributions. FSA and commuter benefits are not PolicyEngine inputs and rest on the state starting from federal income. Not read in the state's own instructions. No employee payroll contribution: the US Department of Labor's comparison lists worker unemployment contributions only in Alaska, New Jersey and Pennsylvania and disability insurance only in California, Hawaii, New Jersey, New York and Rhode Island, and no paid leave or similar program with an employee contribution was found for this state on 2026-11-12.
notes: Ohio municipalities levy their own income taxes on wages and many school districts levy an income tax on residents. Not modeled.
Not modeled: the joint filing credit for married couples, 5% to 20% of tax depending on income, capped at $650.
Ohio has no standard deduction. Business income is taxed separately at a flat 3% and is not covered here.
maintainerNotes: Not modeled: the joint filing credit for married couples filing jointly (it has income conditions that were not read here). PolicyEngine records it as 20%, 15%, 10% or 5% of tax depending on income, capped at $650, and unavailable at modified AGI of $500,000 or more from 2026.
